standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic planning and materials task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With real permission already granted for a specific project, the learner turns the approved scope into an ordered list of concrete steps and a matching list of the real materials each step needs, checking the household for what is already available.

simulationAlternative.description: If permission for the specific project has not yet been finalized, the learner instead plans the ordered steps and materials list for the example need chosen during the diagnostic lesson, treating it as a complete trial plan ready to use once permission is granted.

materials: learner-local: the approved project scope from the previous lesson
adult-or-local: access to the household's existing supplies or tools relevant to the project

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain which part of planning this project — the ordered steps or the materials check — revealed something you hadn't thought of when you first identified the need, and what it was.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner estimate roughly how much total time the whole ordered list of steps will take and compare that estimate to the time estimate they gave a trusted adult during the permission conversation, noting any mismatch.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic planning and materials task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the approved project scope from the previous lesson
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: access to the household's existing supplies or tools relevant to the project
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: planning and materials worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With real permission already granted for a specific project, the learner turns the approved scope into an ordered list of concrete steps and a matching list of the real materials each step needs, checking the household for what is already available.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact planning and materials decision or action.
Model move 2: Before listing steps, picture doing the whole project from start to finish in your head.
Model move 3: Write the project as an ordered list of at least five concrete steps, from first action to last, and note any step that depends on another step being finished first.

Model check: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check.

resources.title: planning and materials action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for planning and materials.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: planning and materials coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With real permission already granted for a specific project, the learner turns the approved scope into an ordered list of concrete steps and a matching list of the real materials each step needs, checking the household for what is already available.
Coach direction: Before listing steps, picture doing the whole project from start to finish in your head.
Learner prompt: Name the very first physical action you would take to start this project, and the very last action that would mean it's finished.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: planning and materials complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Write the project as an ordered list of at least five concrete steps, from first action to last, and note any step that depends on another step being finished first.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My list has at least five steps in a clear order, not a jumbled set of tasks.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I marked which steps must happen before others, if any.

Equal-access rule: If permission for the specific project has not yet been finalized, the learner instead plans the ordered steps and materials list for the example need chosen during the diagnostic lesson, treating it as a complete trial plan ready to use once permission is granted.

resources.title: planning and materials minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain which part of planning this project — the ordered steps or the materials check — revealed something you hadn't thought of when you first identified the need, and what it was.

Success checks: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: planning and materials supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional planning and materials condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

resources.title: planning and materials delivered plan
resources.purpose: Resolves the lesson's named plan so the learner is never directed to a phantom material.
content: Starting information: With real permission already granted for a specific project, the learner turns the approved scope into an ordered list of concrete steps and a matching list of the real materials each step needs, checking the household for what is already available.
Use steps: Write the project as an ordered list of at least five concrete steps, from first action to last, and note any step that depends on another step being finished first.
Field 1 (t2-p1): My list has at least five steps in a clear order, not a jumbled set of tasks.
Field 2 (t2-p2): I marked which steps must happen before others, if any.

Check against: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: With real permission already granted for a specific project, the learner turns the approved scope into an ordered list of concrete steps and a matching list of the real materials each step needs, checking the household for what is already available.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the very first physical action you would take to start this project, and the very last action that would mean it's finished.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: planning and materials — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Write the project as an ordered list of at least five concrete steps, from first action to last, and note any step that depends on another step being finished first.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: planning and materials — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If permission for the specific project has not yet been finalized, the learner instead plans the ordered steps and materials list for the example need chosen during the diagnostic lesson, treating it as a complete trial plan ready to use once permission is granted.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain which part of planning this project — the ordered steps or the materials check — revealed something you hadn't thought of when you first identified the need, and what it was.
observableCriteria: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence.
Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Step sequencing: At least five concrete steps are listed in a workable, ordered sequence. | Materials accuracy: Specific materials are listed for each step that needs one, and each is correctly marked available or missing based on a real household check.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
